items.item: Performance testing and capture metrics
items.notes: Real encrypt/decrypt latency/throughput numbers now exist: a Gatling load-test harness (EncryptDecryptLoadSimulation, com.hsm.core.loadtest, hsm-core-service/src/test/java) drives single- and batch-item encrypt+decrypt round trips against a running instance over real HTTP. Chosen over k6 specifically to avoid introducing a non-JVM binary into this repo's otherwise Java/Maven-only tooling -- Gatling is a plain Maven test-scoped dependency (gatling-charts-highcharts), its own self-contained HTML report needs no extra infra (Prometheus/Grafana) to view, and it follows the same JVM-harness precedent hsm-bulk-service's BulkVsBatchBenchmark already established. gatling-maven-plugin is deliberately bound to no lifecycle phase, so it never runs during mvn test/package, only via `scripts/run-load-test.sh` or `mvn gatling:test` against an already-running service. A real measurement pass (demo mode, MockKekClient/H2, 20 single-item + 5 batch(20-item) virtual users, 10s ramp/30s hold): 1,550 requests, 0 failures, mean 7ms, p95 25ms, p99 48ms, 38.75 req/s combined throughput. See java/docs/PERFORMANCE_TESTING.md for the full writeup, caveats (demo-mode numbers, not real-Managed-HSM/Postgres; batch throughput capped by hsm.service.batch-executor-pool-size=1 by design, not a Gatling-side bottleneck), and tuning knobs. HSM unwrap call volume under concurrency and DEK cache hit ratio under hot-key/bulk patterns are answerable with this same harness but not separately broken out yet. Ongoing/production metrics capture (Micrometer + Actuator, for continuous observability rather than one-off measurement) is a distinct, still-open item -- see the new Backlog entry below.

items.item: Add Actuator + Micrometer for ongoing production metrics

items.item: hsm-bulk-client (CLNT) -- standalone Bulk DB + Bulk File client
items.notes: New module, genuinely separate from SVC (not merged) -- calls POST /dek/issue|unwrap over HTTP, does all AES-GCM locally, no server-side machinery of its own (no auth filter, no JPA). BULK DB: config-driven source/target table+column mapping, independently addressable JDBC URL/schema/table per side, one DEK per column value (not per row), keyset-paginated reads. BULK File: source/target each independently local disk or ADLS (FileStore interface -- mixed pairs like ADLS-to-disk fall out for free), one DEK per whole file, chunks stitched via length-prefixed binary framing (not newline-delimited -- ciphertext can contain a literal 0x0A). Verified live end-to-end against real hsm-core-service + hsm-bulk-service: BULK DB and BULK File round trips both byte-for-byte identical, including a spot-check through hsm-core-service's real /decrypt and a multi-chunk (8-chunk) binary file. Answers BULK_OPERATIONS.md's open 'reference client library' question -- this is that client, not a separate future item.

items.item: hsm-core-service: stop embedding DB credentials in DATABASE_URL
items.notes: hsm-core-service previously expected credentials embedded directly in DATABASE_URL (postgresql://user:pass@host/db) -- but Hikari and Hibernate both print the JDBC URL at startup unconditionally ('Database JDBC URL [...]', 'HikariPool-1 - Added connection ... url=...'), which ships to Splunk via this service's own log pipeline; an embedded password would land in plaintext in every pod's logs. Fixed by adding separate DATABASE_USERNAME/DATABASE_PASSWORD properties (matching hsm-bulk-service's and application-demo.yml's existing pattern), updated helm/hsm-core-service's Secret template accordingly. Verified: hsm-core-service still starts and passes its health check with the new fields; 55/55 tests still pass.

items.item: DEK naming/reuse -- dek_name on /encrypt, /encrypt/batch, /dek/issue
items.notes: Optional dek_name lets a caller reuse the current DEK for (app_id, dek_name) instead of minting one per call -- opt-in, default behavior unchanged. V7 migration adds edek_records.dek_name (permanent) + current_dek_name (nulled on rotation, uniquely indexed per app_id via a shadow-column pair since H2 rejects Postgres's partial-unique-index syntax). Mirrored in EncryptionService.resolveDek (primes DekCache on reuse) and DekIssueService.issueOne (no DekCache there, still one HSM unwrap per reuse but far fewer DEKs minted). Fingerprint left null on named rows -- one edek_id gets many iv/tag pairs under reuse; the existing null-gated check needed no changes. Classification bound per-name: explicit conflict rejects (422), blank-value backfills, blank-blank is a no-op. Fixed a bug: dek_name sent as '' broke the unique index on the next unnamed call -- normalized blank-to-null in both DTOs. Reverses BULK_OPERATIONS.md's 'DEK-per-record, non-negotiable' rejection as a narrow, opt-in exception. 59/59 + 9/9 tests pass.

items.item: Named-DEK rotation scheduler (age-based, hsm-core-service)
items.notes: NamedDekRotationScheduler mirrors KekRotationScheduler's shape (@PostConstruct + CronTrigger, demo-mode guard). RotationService.rotateNamedDeks(maxAgeHours) sweeps current-status edek_records rows with a non-null current_dek_name older than the threshold (default 720h/30d, hsm.named-dek-rotation.*), mints a fresh DEK per row, retires the old one (rotated, current_dek_name cleared, dek_name kept for history). Deliberately time-based, not usage-count-based -- hsm-core-service has no visibility into how many values a caller encrypts with a DEK it hands out (that happens client-side), so a lookup counter could never be trustworthy. One real gotcha: the old row's UPDATE must be saveAndFlush'd before the new row's INSERT, since Hibernate's default flush order is by operation type (inserts before updates), not registration order -- inserting first would transiently violate the unique index within the same transaction. Verified via a dedicated integration test exercising a full rotation round trip.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: Azure AD Workload Identity auth for long-running jobs
items.notes: Previously SvcClient sent a single static config token for a whole job run -- fine for demo mode's never-expiring fixed strings, but a real Azure AD JWT (~1h TTL) would expire mid-run on any job longer than that. New TokenProvider abstraction: StaticTokenProvider (today's behavior, default svc.auth-mode: STATIC) or AzureAdTokenProvider (svc.auth-mode: AZURE_AD), which calls TokenCredential.getToken() fresh before every request -- a cache hit on nearly every call since the Azure Identity SDK caches internally and only re-acquires near expiry, so no manual TTL tracking needed. Same Workload Identity -> Managed Identity -> DefaultAzureCredential cascade already used by AzureKeyVaultKekClient and AdlsFileStore, kept as its own copy per this repo's no-shared-library convention. No client secret anywhere in the chain.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: DbBulkJob named-DEK batching + unwrap dedup
items.notes: ClientProperties.Db.ColumnMapping gained dekName -- DbBulkJob.encrypt() resolves a named column's DEK once for the whole job run (issueNamedColumnDeks(), before the pagination loop starts), not per row or per sub-batch. decrypt() separately dedups by edek_id (not the existing per-row correlation key) before both the /dek/unwrap call and the local RSA-OAEP unwrap -- the RSA step, not the HTTP round trip, was the dominant cost in the original bulk-vs-batch benchmark, so deduping only the network call would have missed the larger win.

items.item: app_decrypt_grants: per-dek_name grant scoping
items.notes: app_decrypt_grants is app-to-app only ((grantee_app_id, owner_app_id), no column/name scoping) -- this predates dek_name and was already this coarse for ordinary DEK-per-record data, so it's not a new gap in kind. But dek_name now gives the system a real taxonomy (customers.ssn vs. customers.account_number) that grant scoping could use but doesn't -- an auditor could reasonably ask why access control doesn't distinguish what DEK issuance already does. Natural fix: extend AppDecryptGrant's key with an optional, nullable dek_name (NULL = today's blanket grant, unchanged; a value scopes to just that name). Not required to ship dek_name reuse itself -- tracked separately.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: DbBulkJob connection pooling, batch-insert fix, and parallelism
items.notes: Prompted by a real report: a 2M-row, 4-column db encrypt job took 4 hours. Root causes, diagnosed against the actual reported config, not guesswork: DriverManagerDataSource (unpooled -- every JDBC op pays full connection-setup cost) and subChunkByItemCap capping insert batches to dek-batch-max-items even when no /dek/issue HTTP call remained to cap. Fixed: HikariDataSource (pool sized to parallelism+2), reWriteBatchedInserts=true auto-appended to Postgres URLs, subChunkByItemCap returns the whole page as one chunk when columnsPerRow=0. New client.db.parallelism (default 1, unchanged): partitions the key range via a bounded, one-time set of OFFSET boundary lookups (not per-page OFFSET, which this design still avoids), one worker per partition. Verified against real Postgres: 9,973-row table split into 4 partitions (2494/2493/2493/2493), every id seen exactly once under real concurrent access.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: DbBulkJob checkpoint/resume
items.notes: New client.db.checkpoint (enabled/resume/job-id/table-name, default disabled -- zero overhead unless opted in). A batch's data insert and its checkpoint update commit in one transaction (TransactionTemplate/DataSourceTransactionManager), so a resumed run can never skip un-written rows nor re-process written ones. Deliberately not built on an ON CONFLICT upsert against the actual target table -- the checkpoint table owns its own guaranteed-unique job_id key, so resume works without requiring the source/target key to be provably unique. Under parallelism>1 each partition gets its own derived checkpoint (job-id-p0, p1...). Verified against real Postgres, 12 checks including a simulated mid-transaction crash: confirmed neither the data row nor the checkpoint landed; a real commit landed both; a second batch upserted (not duplicated) the checkpoint row.

items.item: hsm-bulk-service: Named-DEK rotation scheduler
items.notes: Closes a real, previously-unflagged gap: DEKs issued via POST /dek/issue with a name (DbBulkJob's per-column dek-name, and the new File-job dek-name below) had no rotation at all -- unlike hsm-core-service's own /encrypt dek_name path. New NamedDekRotationScheduler/RotationService, mirroring hsm-core-service's exactly (hsm.named-dek-rotation.*, same age-based reasoning, same saveAndFlush-before-save Hibernate flush-order fix). Verified booting the real Spring app against real Postgres, 13 checks: old row retires (rotated, current_dek_name cleared, wrapped form untouched and still decryptable), a fresh row takes over reuse under the same name, and -- importantly -- a freshly-rotated-in row is NOT re-swept under a realistic 24h cutoff, confirming the age-based logic actually discriminates, not just that the sweep runs.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: FileBulkJob dek-name, parallelism, checkpoint/resume, and decrypt dedup fix
items.notes: client.file.dek-name mirrors DbBulkJob's dek-name but scoped to the whole job (one business purpose, e.g. all-customer-files), not a column -- and persists across every future run, which is why the rotation scheduler above had to exist first. client.file.parallelism splits the file list into even groups (files are independent/unordered, no boundary-key math needed). client.file.checkpoint uses a single batched manifest file in the target store (no per-file marker -- doubles ADLS operation cost; no new DB dependency); flush-interval (default 1000) decoupled from files-per-batch after measuring the coupling cost directly (58s to 10.9s on 60k files, 6000 to 60 rewrites). Found and fixed while verifying: decrypt wasn't deduping by edek_id like DbBulkJob's decrypt does. Verified with a genuine kill -9 mid-run on 60,000 real files: resumed to exactly 60,000/60,000 files/manifest entries, zero duplicates; dek_issued showed 1 event not 60,000; decrypted output byte-for-byte identical to source.

items.item: Tier 3 security/crypto review -- now spans two shared-DEK surfaces, not one
items.notes: Already-open item (see BULK_OPERATIONS.md Open Decisions) made more pressing by this round: dek-name now also exists on the File job, scoped to a whole job/business purpose rather than a single DB column -- a coarser, larger blast radius per name than the DB case (one column is one kind of data; one file job can span many kinds of content under one source tree). Real code exists and is verified working end-to-end for both surfaces; the dedicated security/crypto review this doc has called for since before any of Tier 3 was built has still not happened.

items.item: Operational robustness round: checkpoint CREATE-privilege fix, Hikari pool size, manifest-exclusion fix, client-secret auth
items.notes: Four real environment issues fixed in one round. CheckpointStore: Postgres checks CREATE privilege before table existence, so CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS still fails for a role with only object-level grants on a DBA-pre-created checkpoint table -- fixed via to_regclass existence check first. hsm-bulk-service's Hikari pool was on Spring Boot's default of 10 -- now DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE (default 20). FileStore.list() had no exclusion for FileCheckpointStore's own manifest dir -- a decrypt job could try to decrypt its own manifest as data, failing with EDEK not found. AzureKeyVaultKekClient's credential chain unconditionally fell into Managed-Identity-via-IMDS once client-id was set, even for a Workload-Identity-only identity -- new explicit ClientSecretCredential branch added, both services. Verified against real Postgres, live Hikari config (maximumPoolSize=20 confirmed), and a real encrypt/decrypt cycle reproducing then fixing the manifest bug.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: DB/File decrypt-side persistent DEK cache + sub-chunking fix
items.notes: Root cause of a real 'db decrypt is very slow' / '8x slower than encrypt' report. The existing dedup-by-edek_id only worked within one sub-batch -- the unwrapped DEK was zeroed at batch end and never reused, so a dek-name'd column/job still paid one redundant /dek/unwrap call and RSA-OAEP-256 unwrap (the dominant cost per the earlier benchmark) per batch, for the whole run. Fixed with a persistent cache shared across every partition worker, gated on config (DbBulkJob: per-column dek-name; FileBulkJob: the job's own dek-name) so a genuinely one-off DEK is never cached. Second bug found via a real follow-up report: decryptRange's sub-chunking still capped batch size using the total column count regardless of naming, unlike encryptRange -- fixed to mirror it exactly. Verified live: DbBulkJob (300 rows/30 forced sub-batches -> 1 unwrap event; 5,000 rows/250 forced sub-batches -> 5, one per page, 315ms) and FileBulkJob (60 files/12 forced sub-batches -> 1 unwrap event), all data round-tripped correctly.

items.item: Client IP resolution: honor X-Forwarded-For
items.notes: caller_ip in audit logs and JwtAppIdAuthenticationFilter previously read request.getRemoteAddr() only -- correct for a direct connection, but behind any reverse proxy/gateway (the real deployment topology) it always logs the proxy IP, never the originating caller. New ClientIpResolver takes the first entry of X-Forwarded-For when present (the originating caller, per RFC 7239 convention -- later entries are intermediate hops), falling back to getRemoteAddr() otherwise. Applied consistently in EncryptController, DecryptController (single + batch), and JwtAppIdAuthenticationFilter's own auth-failure audit path. Caveat documented, not fixed here: relies on the edge overwriting the header unconditionally, not appending unconditionally trusted client input -- a spoofing risk if that assumption doesn't hold at the actual network edge.

items.item: Per-request correlation ID (CorrelationIdFilter)
items.notes: New OncePerRequestFilter assigns one correlation ID per request -- reused from an incoming X-Correlation-Id header if the caller supplied one, otherwise a fresh UUID. Placed in MDC (thread-bound, always cleared in a finally block to avoid leaking across pooled threads) before the rest of the filter chain runs, so every plain log line for that request carries it automatically via logging.pattern.level (application.yml's "%5p [correlationId=%X{correlationId:-}]"), with zero call-site plumbing. Echoed back on the X-Correlation-Id response header. Registered ahead of JwtAppIdAuthenticationFilter in SecurityConfig so even an authentication failure's audit/log entries carry a correlation ID. Verified live end-to-end with a caller-supplied ID threading through encrypt_request_received/resolve_dek_*/component_call_*/encrypt_request_completed.

items.item: Request/collaborator timing observability: manual timers + Spring AOP
items.notes: Three layers, chosen per what proxy-based Spring AOP can and cannot intercept (it wraps Spring-managed bean instances and only sees calls crossing a bean boundary -- not private methods, not self-invocation, not static calls on a non-bean utility class). (1) EncryptionService.encrypt() logs encrypt_request_received/encrypt_request_completed total_duration_ms around the whole request -- plain manual timer, not AOP-able since it is the entry method itself. (2) resolve_dek_started/resolve_dek_completed duration_ms around resolveDek() -- also manual, since it is a private method called via self-invocation, which an AOP proxy cannot see. (3) New ComponentTimingAspect (com.hsm.core.aop, spring-boot-starter-aop dependency) with @Around advice on PbacClient.check, KekClient.wrapDek/unwrapDek, and EdekRecordRepository.save -- these four ARE cleanly AOP-able since each sits behind an interface implemented by a distinct Spring bean, called from a different bean than the one invoking it. Logs component_call_started/component_call_completed component=<..> method=<..> duration_ms=<n> status=success|error. DekManager (a static utility on a non-bean final class) is not AOP-covered for the same underlying reason as resolveDek. Verified live: a slow request now shows exactly which collaborator (PBAC check, KEK wrap/unwrap, EDEK save, or DEK resolution) the time went to, not just an opaque overall duration.

items.item: Bounded concurrent batch processing (encrypt/decrypt batch)
items.notes: encryptBatch/decryptBatch previously ran items in a strict sequential for-loop -- deliberate, per BULK_OPERATIONS.md's documented concern about self-inflicted HSM throttling from uncontrolled fan-out with no real Managed HSM throughput numbers to size a worker pool by. New BatchExecutorConfig adds one shared, pod-wide ExecutorService bean sized by hsm.service.batch-executor-pool-size (BATCH_EXECUTOR_POOL_SIZE env var, default "1" -- an aggregate cap on concurrent HSM-bound calls across every batch request in the pod, not a per-batch worker count, and default 1 reproduces the exact original sequential behavior with zero change until deliberately raised). Item results are still collected back in original submission order regardless of completion order, and per-item error isolation is unchanged (encryptBatchItem/decryptBatchItem catch ApiException/RuntimeException per item exactly as the old inline try/catch did). New MdcPropagatingCallable explicitly copies the submitting thread's MDC (correlation ID) onto each pooled worker thread before running and restores it after -- found live during verification that without this, every batch item's log lines silently lost their correlation ID the moment work moved off the original HTTP request thread, undermining the correlation-ID work above for exactly the traffic (batches) most likely to need it. Also fixed in the same round: MockKekClient.unwrapDek() had an unsynchronized read of its versions map racing rotateToNewVersion()'s lock-protected write -- harmless only while nothing ever called into this class concurrently, a real (if rare) bug the moment any concurrency exists. Verified live: batch items observed running on shared batch-executor-N threads (not per-request threads), correlation ID present on every item log line, and one malformed item in a mixed batch failing independently without affecting the other item's success.

items.item: Additive response envelope on /encrypt and /decrypt
items.notes: EncryptResponse and DecryptResponse gained four new trailing fields -- status, code, message, correlation_id -- with every existing field (ciphertext_token, edek_id, plaintext, etc.) left completely unchanged, no rename. Deliberately additive rather than a versioned endpoint or a literal field rename: the demo UI's app.js references ciphertext_token by that exact name in four places, and a rename would have broken it for no compensating benefit. correlationId is read from MDC (CorrelationIdFilter.MDC_KEY, made public specifically so this code could reference the same key without duplicating the literal) so it matches the X-Correlation-Id response header exactly. No referenceId field added -- that has nothing to reference until true async batch processing (job tracking, a caller polling a job ID) exists, which is a separate, larger, still-unbuilt change; shipping an always-null field now would be worse than omitting it. Error responses (4xx/5xx) are unchanged, still {"detail": "..."} via GlobalExceptionHandler -- this round only touches the success-path body shape. Verified live via curl for both /encrypt and /decrypt.

items.item: Literal field rename: ciphertext_token -> ciphertext, across the board
items.notes: Supersedes the earlier additive-envelope round's explicit "no rename" decision -- an explicit follow-up instruction chose to apply the rename anyway, breaking-change tradeoffs accepted. Scope: EncryptResponse/DecryptRequest/BatchDecryptItem/ConsumerAccountResponse (hsm-core-service DTOs), ConsumerAccount JPA entity + a new V9 Flyway migration (ALTER TABLE consumer_customer_accounts RENAME COLUMN ciphertext_token TO ciphertext -- V3's original migration is untouched, Flyway history is immutable), DecryptionService/DemoController call sites and error-message strings, all three duplicated DekManager.java copies (core/bulk-service/bulk-client) error messages and comments, hsm-bulk-service's BulkVsBatchBenchmark (posts directly to hsm-core-service's /decrypt, would have started failing otherwise), hsm-bulk-client terminology (DbBulkJob/ClientProperties javadoc, application.yml + both config-examples' suggested column-naming convention -- these don't touch a real wire contract since bulk-client talks to hsm-bulk-service's separate /dek/issue //dek/unwrap contract, updated for consistency only), the demo UI (app.js FIELD_EXPLAINERS key + 3 accessor call sites, index.html's Consumer Table description/column-plan table/inline architecture+sequence diagram SVG text -- 8 places), all 4 integration test files, both standalone diagram SVGs (docs/architecture-diagram.svg, docs/sequence-diagram.svg), and BULK_OPERATIONS.md/RUNBOOK.md/TIER3_POC_BUILD.md/docs/DEMO.md. Deliberately left untouched: legacy ciphertext_b64 field (unrelated, a different deprecated field), V3's original migration text, RUNBOOK.md's and EncryptDecryptIntegrationTest.java's own historical references to the old name, the two pre-existing dev-status-seed.json entries documenting the earlier round's reasoning at the time it was made, and the legacy Python app/ tree (out of scope, separate deletion decision still pending). Full reactor compile + hsm-core-service test suite passing; new V9 migration applies cleanly against the live demo H2 DB's existing data; verified live via curl and in-browser against the demo UI.
